evidence: nagios-may-run-it-through-sudo: manifests/sysmon_fs_health.pp:10 declares sudo::conf priority 10 with content 'nagios ALL=NOPASSWD:${bindir}/${scriptname}'; with bindir /opt/puppet-infrastructure/bin (lab Hiera) and title sysmon_fs_health the probe greps exactly that line in /etc/sudoers.d/10_nagios_fs_health_sysmon_fs_health and confirms visudo -c; supported

check-script-rendered: manifests/sysmon_fs_health.pp:13-16 declare the script root/root 0755 from check-fs-health.sh.erb, whose lines 8-10 render BASEDIR/SIZE_THRESHOLD/NFILES from the params (/var/tmp/p8test-fs-health, 8, 3); probe checks owner root, mode 755, bash -n, and those three rendered values; supported

check-reports-ok-on-a-healthy-tree: template 96-97 print 'OK: exit code $RC $OUTPUT' and exit 0 once check_size (du -sk > 8; five 4 KB files give about 24) and check_files/check_files_content pass; OUTPUT is never set, so 'OK: exit code 0 ' with the trailing space and rc=0 is what the code produces; the action only creates the tree (its mutates text also says it runs the script, which the read-only effect does: an over-declaration, harmless); supported

purpose gap: Covered: the rendered per-volume script and the sudoers drop-in (manifest 3-17), CRITICAL 'storage space is empty' rc 2 on an empty tree (template 42-52, 80-83), OK rc 0 on a healthy tree as root and as nagios through sudo -n (54-97); purpose statement matches the manifest and template. GAP: the outcome 'a file whose content cannot be read is reported CRITICAL' (template 63-74, handle_error 'error checking md5sum for $f') is marked uncovered with why 'the script runs as root, only an I/O error on the volume makes find or md5sum fail' and evidence 'phase3.py has no fault-injection step'. Neither holds: on puppet8node (read-only via lab_exec) /sys/bus/pci/rescan is a regular file (find -type f lists it, mode --w-------) and 'sudo md5sum /sys/bus/pci/rescan' fails rc 1 'Permission denied' as root, so a mutating check that bind-mounts such a file into a tree with at most NFILES=3 regular files (size still > 8 KB) deterministically hits that CRITICAL branch; dmsetup, losetup and mkfs.ext4 are also present on the node for an error-target volume. phase3 mutating actions run arbitrary root commands, so the evidence does not show the lab lacking a capability. Note (not counted): nagios-runs-the-check-through-sudo has no mismatch control (another user through sudo -n must fail), and its effect is the action's captured output.
